contracts.basis: NL1 clause 'Once the device is powered on, the system enters the Operate state'.

binding_hints.basis: NL1 'Once the device is powered on'
binding_hints.reason: The device's pre-power-on state is the implicit source of this transition.

binding_hints.basis: NL1 'the system enters the Operate state'
binding_hints.reason: Operate is the explicit named target state entered upon power-on.

contracts.normative_statement: When the device is powered on, the system must transition from the off/root state to the Operate state.
contracts.quote: Once the device is powered on, the system enters the `Operate` state
contracts.reason: NL1 explicitly states the system enters Operate upon power-on, establishing a source-target transition obligation from an implicit off/root source to Operate.
contracts.scope: Root-level power-on transition into Operate

contracts.basis: NL1 'it transitions between Idle, Accelerating or Cruising, and Braking states' following the Operate-entry clause.

binding_hints.basis: NL1 preceding clause establishing Operate as the entered state
binding_hints.reason: Operate is the enclosing composite whose substates are being enumerated.
Idle is named as one substate of Operate.
Accelerating is named as one substate of Operate.
Cruising is named as one substate of Operate.
Braking is named as one substate of Operate.

contracts.normative_statement: Idle, Accelerating, Cruising, and Braking must each be contained as substates within the Operate state.
contracts.quote: based on user actions, it transitions between `Idle`, `Accelerating or Cruising`, and `Braking` states
contracts.reason: NL1 lists Idle, Accelerating, Cruising, and Braking as the states among which the system transitions while in Operate, establishing them as Operate's substates.
contracts.scope: Operate composite substate membership

contracts.basis: NL1 establishes Operate as owner of Idle/Accelerating/Cruising/Braking and that the system enters Operate then moves among these states.

binding_hints.basis: NL1 clause establishing Operate as the entered composite
binding_hints.reason: Operate owns the required initial pseudostate edge into its substates.

binding_hints.basis: NL1 substate enumeration 'Idle, Accelerating or Cruising, and Braking'
binding_hints.reason: Idle is the most plausible default/initial substate given its naming as a rest state, though NL leaves this open; preserved as the initial-entry target candidate.

contracts.normative_statement: Within Operate, the system must have a defined initial substate entry among Idle, Accelerating, Cruising, or Braking (discourse establishes Idle as the natural starting substate once Operate is entered).
contracts.quote: the system enters the `Operate` state, and based on user actions, it transitions between `Idle`, `Accelerating or Cruising`, and `Braking` states
contracts.reason: Once Operate is entered as an owner composite with enumerated substates, discourse implies an owner-local initial-entry obligation into one of those substates (Idle being the natural rest/default state); this preserves the initial_entry property distinct from the root transition into Operate.
contracts.scope: Operate-owned initial substate entry

contracts.basis: NL2 'The system can be turned on with the start signal'.

binding_hints.basis: NL2 'turned on with the start signal'
binding_hints.reason: The off state is the implicit source before the start signal is received.

binding_hints.basis: NL2 combined with NL1 'the system enters the Operate state'
binding_hints.reason: Operate is the destination entered upon receiving the start signal, consistent with NL1.
start is the explicit named signal causing this transition.

contracts.normative_statement: On the start signal, the system must transition from the off/root state to the Operate state.
contracts.quote: The system can be turned on with the `start` signal
contracts.reason: NL2 names the exact trigger (start) that causes power-on entry into Operate, refining the endpoint established in NL1 with an explicit event.
contracts.scope: Power-on transition triggered by start signal

contracts.basis: NL2 'turned off with the keyOff signal'.

binding_hints.basis: NL2 'turned off' implies exit from the currently active Operate state
binding_hints.reason: Operate is the source state from which the system exits upon keyOff.

binding_hints.basis: NL2 'turned off with the keyOff signal'
binding_hints.reason: The off state is the destination reached upon receiving keyOff.
keyOff is the explicit named signal causing this transition.

contracts.normative_statement: On the keyOff signal, the system must transition from the Operate state to the off/root state.
contracts.quote: and turned off with the `keyOff` signal
contracts.reason: NL2 names the exact trigger (keyOff) that causes exit from Operate back to the off/root state, an independent endpoint from the power-on transition.
contracts.scope: Power-off transition triggered by keyOff signal

contracts.basis: NL2 'turned off with the keyOff signal' combined with NL1/NL3 establishing Operate as an owner scope with active substates.

binding_hints.reason: keyOff is the exact event required to be consumable throughout the scope.

binding_hints.basis: NL1 establishing Operate as the owning composite of active substates
binding_hints.reason: Operate and its substates form the scope within which keyOff must be accepted.

contracts.normative_statement: The keyOff signal must be accepted throughout the Operate scope so the system can always be turned off.
contracts.quote: The system can be turned on with the `start` signal and turned off with the `keyOff` signal.
contracts.reason: NL2 states the system can be turned off with keyOff at any time while operating, which is a coverage obligation that keyOff must be consumable from within Operate and its substates, not merely at one specific substate.
contracts.scope: keyOff acceptance across Operate and its substates

contracts.basis: NL3 'Within the Operate state, the system transitions between different substates depending on actions like accelerating, braking, or stopping.'

binding_hints.reason: Operate is explicitly named as the enclosing scope for these substate transitions.
Accelerating substate is implicated by the 'accelerating' action.
Braking substate is implicated by the 'braking' action.
Idle substate is implicated by the 'stopping' action.

contracts.normative_statement: The substates involved in accelerating, braking, and stopping actions must be contained within the Operate state.
contracts.quote: Within the `Operate` state, the system transitions between different substates depending on actions like accelerating, braking, or stopping.
contracts.reason: NL3 reaffirms that substates reached via accelerating, braking, and stopping actions are within Operate, reinforcing the containment obligation already established in NL1 but attaching it to this exact segment so NL3 is covered by an independent atomic contract.
contracts.scope: Operate composite substate membership (reinforced)

contracts.basis: NL3 'depending on actions like accelerating, braking, or stopping' lists mutually distinguishing alternatives.

binding_hints.reason: Preserves the exact set of distinguishing alternatives named by NL3.
binding_hints.value: accelerating vs braking vs stopping action selection

contracts.normative_statement: The accelerating, braking, and stopping actions must select mutually exclusive/distinguishable substate transitions within Operate.
contracts.quote: the system transitions between different substates depending on actions like accelerating, braking, or stopping
contracts.reason: NL3 explicitly presents accelerating, braking, and stopping as distinct alternative causes for substate transitions from a shared context (within Operate); the alternatives are semantically intended to be distinguishable so the correct substate transition fires for each action.
contracts.scope: Alternative substate transitions inside Operate selected by distinct user actions

response.reason: NL1 establishes root-level containment (Operate as entered state), an initial-entry-like transition from power-on to Operate, and a shared-source transition group among Idle/Accelerating/Cruising/Braking substates. NL3 restates that within Operate the system moves among substates depending on actions, reinforcing the transition group and substate containment already captured under NL1, so it is marked covered by reusing/extending containment and transition-group contracts tied to NL3's segment id as well.

The FCSTM adds an off-source `Off -> Terminate` unconditional transition (no NL basis) and an `Operate -> Off` guarded exit conditioned on a route-token variable rather than the direct `keyOff` trigger described by NL. Terminate is a reachable leaf with zero outgoing transitions (LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING / W_DEADLOCK_LEAF), which is a deterministic dead-end fact on a state absent from any NL contract locus, so it is not tied to any supplied contract and is not emitted as a candidate here; instead it is reported only insofar as it affects the NL2-ENDPOINT-2/EVTCOV contracts' downstream keyOff semantics. keyOff is declared and reachable-consumed inside Operate (Idle/AcceleratingOrCruising/Braking all fire transition:line:16/17/18), satisfying NL2-EVTCOV-1's reachable-consumer coverage. I flag this via NL2-ENDPOINT-2 with wrong_guard-adjacent observation (kept as mismatched/wrong_target direction consistent with contract) since the direct edge's trigger no longer literally carries keyOff (it's carried on the internal Idle/AccelOrCruising/Braking->[*] edges), and the final relay edge is guard-gated instead of NL's plain requirement. All transition-endpoint contracts for Idle->Accelerating/Cruising/Braking substates are satisfied by tr existing edges (Idle->AcceleratingOrCruising, AcceleratingOrCruising->Braking, Braking->Idle) though the "Cruising" as separate target does not exist -- AcceleratingOrCruising is a single merged state, which is a structural containment mismatch already covered by the complementary contract_structure_contrast lens; here I focus on behavioral consequence: the cyclic substate chain (Idle->AccelOrCruising->Braking->Idle) has no direct branching from Idle to Braking or Idle to Cruising alone, meaning the derived DERIVED-8f88e...
